result.title: Beliefs in feedback: Factored representations of interacting agents in transformers
result.summary: Complex systems, from ecosystems to brains, are usually modeled as modular components coupled through feedback rather than as indivisible wholes. Can a transformer trained on the joint behavior of a group of interacting agents be understood in the same way? In this work, we develop a computational-mechanics framework to study agents interacting in feedback loops. We formally prove that any joint stochastic process can be presented as resulting from the behavior of agents interacting in feedback, and the resulting process is generated by a hidden Markov model whose Bayesian beliefs factorize into separate components per agent. Furthermore, our experiments show that transformers trained on such feedback sequences make use of this separability, disentangling the beliefs about the underlying factors into separate subspaces of their residual stream. This representation is found to scale linearly (instead of exponentially) with the number of agents. Moreover, interventions show that these representations are causally efficacious, allowing for targeted steering of individual agents' beliefs by selectively inserting counterfactuals. However, coarse-graining the behavior is found to disrupt the factorization, and can force a higher-dimensional representation. Together, the results establish both the dimensional advantage of a factorized representation and the ability of transformers to exploit it, laying the groundwork for investigating traces of compositional predictive architecture in pretrained models.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出反馈交互智能体的计算力学框架，证明联合随机过程可由分解为各智能体分量的贝叶斯信念生成，并在 transformer 中发现这些信念被分离到残差流的不同子空间，规模随智能体数量线性增长，且可通过反事实插入进行因果操控。
AI.relevance_reason: 其因子化信念子空间、线性维度优势与干预式因果验证，可供核查 VLM 内部视觉与任务因素是否分离，以及按因子操控 latent 状态；但研究对象是纯文本交互序列，向多模态推理的迁移仍需验证。
